newsitem.title: USA: Group asks U.S. to save endangered world wildlife.
newsitem.headline: Group asks U.S. to save endangered world wildlife.

text.p: The United States should take more aggressive action to save threatened wildlife populations overseas, officials with a government employee activist group said on Tuesday.

Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility (PEER) said it planned to file a petition on Wednesday to the Fish and Wildlife Service to add more than 3,700 foreign animals to the U.S. list for protection under the Endangered Species Act.

The group based its plea on a comprehensive list of endangered animals put out by the World Conservation Union last year, which Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt praised as the most complete scientific study of threatened wildlife.

While the United States cannot require the kinds of habitat protections in foreign countries that it can use at home to save wildlife and plants from dying out, by listing foreign species it can impose trade restrictions.
PEER counsel Jeffrey Ruch said the Fish and Wildlife Service, an arm of the Interior Department, was not doing enough to ban imports of foreign species and their parts in the U.S. market.
"At the current rate (of listing) they would never catch up with what international authorities say is the true state of jeopardy," Ruch said in an interview.

Fish and Wildlife Service spokeswoman Patricia Fisher said with limited resources the agency was trying to "balance the listing of foreign species ... against recognising and supporting successful recovery and management in range countries of these species."
